A: CONSTRUCTION PROJECT APP – GENERAL BUILD REFERENCE | B: Updated general guidance for the developer specification

A: Purpose | B: This workbook section provides shared instructions and reference data used across the construction project app. Each form sheet remains the primary specification for its own fields, dropdowns and workflow.
A: How to use | B: Use the relevant form sheet to build each screen in the stated field order. Use the general sheets only where the form explicitly references them.

A: Source of truth – form classifications | B: NCR Type/Category, Change Order Type/Category, Agreements Type/Category and Lessons Learned Phase/Category are defined in their respective form sheets. Do not create duplicate competing lists in Shared Dropdown Lists.
A: Shared dropdowns | B: Use Shared Dropdown Lists only for values genuinely reused across multiple forms. If a list is specific to one form, maintain it in that form sheet.

A: Works Ongoing and Works Completed | B: Use identical Work discipline and Activity values in both forms. Work discipline is the parent dropdown; Activity is filtered by the selected discipline. When discipline changes, clear the selected activity and any dependent activity-specific responses.

A: Activity Detail Guide | B: After an activity is selected in Works Ongoing or Works Completed, display the relevant prompts from Activity Detail Guide. Use the same activity key (discipline + activity) in both forms. The guide supports activity-specific detail; it does not replace the main work description, location, quantity or status fields.

A: Activity-specific prompts | B: Show only prompts relevant to the selected activity. Store each response against the work record. If an activity changes, clear or revalidate responses that no longer apply. If Other is selected, reveal a required explanation field.
A: Dependent dropdowns | B: For every Type → Category field, filter Category by the selected Type. Clear Category when Type changes. Do not allow a category from another type to remain selected.

A: Project registers | B: Project, location, user, contractor, supplier, crew and linked-record selections must come from live app registers and respect the logged-in user's permissions. Do not hard-code project-specific register data.

A: Required fields | B: Required? = Yes means the field is required at submission, except where a dependency makes it conditionally required. Validate conditional fields only when their trigger applies.
A: Multi-select fields | B: Use multi-select only where specified. Enforce exclusivity rules stated in the form instructions, such as Not Applicable not being combined with other selections.

A: Workflow / permissions | B: Approval, rejection, inspection acceptance, verification and closure actions must be role-restricted. Record user, date/time, previous value and new value in an audit trail.

A: Shared values and local values | B: Where a shared value is used in multiple forms, reference the centrally maintained list. Where a form has a distinct business classification or workflow, keep its list local to that form.

A: Configuration governance | B: Project administrators may maintain lists explicitly marked project-configurable. Changes to controlled classifications should be versioned and should not silently alter historical records.

A: Final implementation check | B: Before go-live, test dependent dropdowns, conditional visibility, required-field validation, linked records, permissions, attachments, audit trails and reporting filters across all forms.

A: Scope note | B: This replacement updates general guidance and shared references only. It does not replace individual form sheets. Insert these sheets into the existing master workbook, replacing sheets with the same names.

A: Sign-off and review workflows | B: Forms requiring signatures use the Sign-off Workflow sheet. Do not use a single static signature field for multi-stage processes. Each submit, acknowledgement, review, return, resubmission, approval and verification is stored as a separate immutable event linked to the form record.

A: Contractor vs supervision signatures | B: Apply the form-specific workflow profile. An acknowledgement of receipt is not automatically acceptance of quality, cost, time, responsibility or liability. Use authorized roles and project-defined approval limits.

A: Final developer handover | B: This workbook is the consolidated build specification. Use the form sheets, general reference sheets and Sign-off Workflow sheet together. Any unresolved project-specific roles, approval limits or legal signature requirements must be confirmed by the project owner before go-live.

A: Technical Instructions classification | B: Instruction Type is an independent dropdown; Discipline uses the same 17 Work discipline values as Works Ongoing / Works Completed; Category is filtered by Discipline. Do not mix Instruction Type with Discipline or workflow status.

A: 6 | B: Incident category | C: Dependent dropdown | D: Yes | E: Near Miss: • Falling / Dropped Object Near Miss — An object fell or was dropped and could have struck a person or caused damage, but did not. • Slip / Trip / Fall Near Miss — A person nearly slipped, tripped or fell, without sustaining an injury. • Vehicle / Equipment Near Collision — A vehicle or machine nearly collided with a person, vehicle, structure or object. • Electrical Near Miss — An electrical event could have caused shock, burn or other harm, but no injury occurred. • Lifting Operation Near Miss — A lifting or rigging event nearly caused injury or damage. • Work-at-Height Near Miss — A person or object was at risk of falling from height, but no injury occurred. • Excavation / Trenching Near Miss — A near collapse, fall into an excavation or utility strike was narrowly avoided. • Fire / Explosion Near Miss — An ignition, gas release or other event could have caused a fire or explosion. • Chemical Release Near Miss — A chemical release or exposure was narrowly avoided or contained without harm. • Structural / Temporary Works Near Miss — A structure, scaffold, formwork or support showed signs of potential failure without collapse or injury. Injury / Illness: • First Aid Case — A work-related injury or illness requiring basic first aid treatment. • Medical Treatment Case — A work-related injury or illness requiring treatment beyond basic first aid. • Lost Time Injury (LTI) — A work-related injury or illness resulting in lost time beyond the day or shift of the event. • Restricted Work Case — A work-related injury or illness resulting in temporary restriction from normal duties. • Occupational Illness — An illness suspected or confirmed to be related to workplace exposure or conditions. • Fatality — A work-related event resulting in death. Property / Equipment Damage: • Building / Structure Damage — An event caused damage to a building, structure, road or other property. • Plant / Machinery Damage — An event caused damage to construction plant, machinery or equipment. • Vehicle Accident / Damage — A vehicle was involved in a collision or sustained damage during an event. • Material / Asset Damage — An event caused damage to stored materials, tools or other project assets. Environmental Incident: • Oil / Fuel Spill — An unintended release of oil, fuel or lubricant to land, water or a drain. • Chemical Spill / Release — An unintended release of a chemical or hazardous substance. • Waste Mismanagement Event — An event resulted in improper release, mixing, loss or disposal of waste. • Wastewater / Sewage Release — An unintended discharge of wastewater or sewage to the environment. • Air Emission / Dust Event — An unintended or uncontrolled emission of smoke, dust, fumes or other pollutants. • Water / Soil Contamination — An event caused or may have caused contamination of water or soil. • Wildlife / Vegetation Impact — An event caused injury to wildlife or damage to vegetation or habitat. Fire / Explosion: • Fire — An unplanned fire occurred on site or involved project activities, equipment or materials. • Explosion — An explosion or blast event occurred, causing or potentially causing harm or damage. • Smoke / Overheating Event — Smoke, overheating or smouldering occurred and required response, even if no fire developed. Vehicle / Traffic Incident: • Vehicle Collision — A vehicle collided with another vehicle, person, structure or object. • Vehicle Rollover — A vehicle or mobile plant overturned during operation or movement. • Pedestrian / Vehicle Contact — A vehicle or mobile plant made contact with a pedestrian. • Reversing Incident — An event occurred while a vehicle or machine was reversing. • Load Shift / Falling Load — A transported load shifted, fell or was released during movement. Other Event: • Security-Related Event — Theft, unauthorized entry, vandalism or another security event affected the site. • Public / Third-Party Incident — A member of the public or third party was affected by a project-related event. • Other HSE Incident — An HSE-related event occurred that does not fit another incident category. | F: Filter categories and show description. A: Purpose | B: Provide reusable, configurable sign-off workflows for forms requiring contractor acknowledgement, supervision review, approval, verification or repeated return/resubmission.

A: Core design rule | B: Do NOT create only one Contractor Signature and one Supervision Signature field. Use a repeatable, append-only Sign-off Event Log linked to each form record. One record can have many actions and many review rounds.

A: Authentication | B: Prefer authenticated user accounts and electronic signatures tied to the user identity. Record server timestamp and audit metadata. A typed name alone is not a secure signature. A: Back-and-forth / review rounds | B: Every Return for Correction action must record mandatory comments, return reason, responsible next actor and due date where applicable. Resubmission creates a new round/event; never overwrite prior comments or signatures. Allow repeated cycles until accepted/closed or withdrawn.

A: Version control | B: Freeze the submitted form version for each review round. If material fields are changed after submission, create a new version and require the relevant approvals again. Preserve previous submitted versions and all sign-off events.

A: Delegation / authority | B: Only authorized roles may approve, reject, accept or close. Configure role permissions and approval limits per project/contract. A user must not approve their own submission unless explicitly allowed by project governance.

A: Notifications | B: Notify the next responsible person/role after submission, return, response, approval, rejection or overdue action. Provide reminders and escalation based on configurable due dates.

A: Record display | B: Show current status, current stage, pending actor/role, last action, last action date and complete chronological sign-off history. Allow authorized users to export the history with the form record.

A: Control | B: Requirement
A: Mandatory comments | B: Require comments for Return, Reject, Reopen and any action that changes responsibility or approval state.

2.1 Navigation principles
Workspace is for creating and submitting forms, not for archiving.
Project Documents contains official project reference information used to execute and supervise the works.
Records & Photos contains records generated during supervision: submitted forms, photos, evidence and history.
